title: Great Gransden (Hayley Wood) Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 7 killed; pilot Plt Off. James Kirkwood
narrative: Lancaster JB219 of 97 Squadron departed Bourn on the night of 16 December 1943, targeting Berlin as part of the Battle of Berlin. On the return flight, the crew encountered the dense fog and low cloud that had settled across southern England — conditions that brought down approximately seventy returning bombers that night in what became known as "Black Thursday." Flying Officer Kirkwood was unable to land safely, and JB219 came down at Hayley Wood, Great Gransden, Cambridgeshire. All seven crew members were killed. The pilot, Flying Officer James Kirkwood DFC, was 28 years old.

crew.name: James Kirkwood
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Lancaster JB219 crashed into Hayley Wood at 00:10 on 17 December 1943, returning from Berlin on 'Black Thursday'. Kirkwood held the DFC.
crew.bio: A 28-year-old pilot and holder of the Distinguished Flying Cross, Kirkwood was the eldest of the crew. He was flying with 97 Squadron, part of No. 8 (Pathfinder) Group.

external_narratives.summary: Comprehensive page on F/O James Kirkwood DFC and crew of Lancaster JB219 OF-R, 97 Squadron. The aircraft crashed at Hayley Wood at 00:10 on 17 December 1943 while returning from Berlin, one of 70 bombers lost to fog on 'Black Thursday'.
external_narratives.key_details: Kirkwood held the DFC. 97 Squadron lost eight Lancasters that night with 36 aircrew killed. The crew ranged in age from 21 to 28. Memorial plaque dedicated on 15 September 2007.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed history and tribute to F/O James Kirkwood DFC and crew of Lancaster JB219 OF-R who tragically lost their lives at Hayley Wood on December 17, 1943.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed article on 'The Night of the Fog' (Black Thursday), 16/17 December 1943. Nearly 500 aircraft attacked Berlin; casualties over the target were light but 70 bombers crashed on return when fog enveloped eastern England.
external_narratives.key_details: 97 Squadron at Bourn suffered the worst losses of the night. Lancaster JB219 completed the Berlin mission successfully but could not find its way through the fog to land.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed article on 'The Night of the Fog' (Black Thursday), 16/17 December 1943, in Lancaster Memorial Archive.

external_narratives.summary: Crew record for F/O Kirkwood's team from the RAF Pathfinders Archive. Documents the crew's service with 97 Squadron and their loss during the Battle of Berlin campaign.
external_narratives.key_details: 97 Squadron was part of No. 8 (Pathfinder) Group. The crew were lost during the sustained Battle of Berlin bombing campaign.
